scope: The badge catalog and badge-centric features: the catalog itself, badge detail pages, rarity, drop and claim windows, owner statistics, badge artwork and metadata, badge discovery and search, and anything that makes the catalog itself more valuable.

ideas.title: Second-source catalog probe
ideas.body: Helix is the official badge source but is not complete: event, regional and legacy sets are missing from it. A low-frequency probe of the badge-sets endpoint the Twitch web client's own badge picker uses diffs against the Helix catalog and proposes missing rows with their art URL and set id, each flagged as a secondary source until the normal sync or a human confirms it. Proposed rows are excluded from feeds and from the rarity math until confirmed. Effort: M. Risk if built badly: an undocumented internal endpoint can change or throttle without notice, and a probe that guesses too much pollutes the authoritative catalog, so results must stay proposals and never auto-insert.
ideas.why: Catalog completeness is the product, and the official API is provably not the entire catalog.

ideas.title: Badge art revision detector
ideas.body: At each sync, hash a downsampled copy of every badge image per set_id and version and store the hash; when the hash changes while the version does not, mark the badge 'art revised' and show an old-versus-new side by side on the detail page with the date it happened. The catalog gains an 'art revised' filter and the change writes its own changelog row. Uses the existing Helix image URLs plus one stored hash column, no new provider needed. Effort: M. Risk if built badly: CDN re-encodes and resize variants change bytes without a real art change, so hashing the downsampled pixels rather than raw bytes is mandatory or the alert becomes permanent noise.
ideas.why: Twitch quietly reissues badge art under the same set and version, and the catalog currently has no idea it happened.

ideas.title: Chat-scale badge preview
ideas.body: A control on each badge page renders the badge the way it truly appears in Twitch chat: at 18 px and 36 px, beside a sample username, on the three chat backgrounds, so a collector can judge whether the art reads at real size. Uses only the catalog image URL and the badge title, and a 'copy chat line' button emits the exact BBCode and HTML shown in the preview. Effort: S. Risk if built badly: if the preview is not pixel-accurate (wrong offset or wrong theme background) it teaches people the opposite of what chat looks like.
ideas.why: Badges live at 18 px in chat while every catalog, including this one, presents them at 28 px and larger.

ideas.title: Claim-path start lag
ideas.body: For each window, measure the gap between the listed opening time and the first owner increase observed in badge_stats, and show it on the badge page as 'first claims tracked 47 minutes after the listed start', with a per-category median and a filter for windows that never delivered a tracked claim. This exposes claim-path delay and quietly broken drops without guessing at Twitch internals. Uses window start dates plus the owner series and sync timestamps. Effort: M. Risk if built badly: a sync that simply ran late makes a window look delayed, so each gap must record how long after the window the observation was actually taken.
ideas.why: A window that opens late or never opens is the difference between a collector claiming a badge and missing it.

ideas.title: Provider page snapshot archive
ideas.body: At first sighting of a badge, and again when its window closes, store the provider page we read it from (HTML plus a rendered screenshot) against the badge, and let the detail page link to that frozen copy with its fetch timestamp. When badgebase or potat later changes or deletes a page, the evidence this site based a window date on still exists and can be diffed against the current one. Storage is small text and one image per badge per event. Effort: M. Risk if built badly: archived third-party pages can contain personal data or tracking scripts, so the snapshot must be sanitized before serving and never rendered with scripts enabled.
ideas.why: A badge database is only as credible as the evidence behind its dates, and provider pages disappear.

ideas.title: Window deadline change log
ideas.body: Record every observed start and end date per window at each sync, so any change becomes a dated event on the badge page ('end moved from 12 Sep to 19 Sep') with the previous value shown, and a catalog filter for badges whose deadline has moved this month. The same history scores providers on how often their first listed end date matched the observed expiry, per category. Effort: M. Risk if built badly: scoring on any reported date rather than the first observed one makes a provider that posts honest corrections look inaccurate, which is the opposite of the truth.
ideas.why: A deadline that moves is the most common way a collector misses a badge, and nothing records the movement today.

ideas.title: Badge name collision pages
ideas.body: Detect catalog rows that share a display title or a near-identical name, and publish a disambiguation page listing them with the distinguishing facts (set_id, category, window, owner count) plus cross-links from each badge page. The search result for an ambiguous query routes to that page instead of picking one arbitrarily. Effort: S. Risk if built badly: an over-eager similarity threshold creates disambiguation pages for badges that are already distinct, so collisions need an exact-title trigger first and fuzzy matching only as a suggestion.
ideas.why: Twitch reuses names like TwitchCon and Prime repeatedly, and the catalog resolves them to whichever row sorted first.

ideas.title: Archived owner-series backfill
ideas.body: A recovery pass pulls dated public snapshots of badge owner pages (Wayback captures of badgebase and potat, plus any other public archives) and inserts the recovered date and owner count into badge_stats marked as source 'archive', with the marker visible on the owner chart. This extends owner curves years earlier than this site has been collecting, so age, rarity and momentum rest on more than a few weeks of observations. Effort: L. Risk if built badly: archive captures are inconsistent and sometimes wrong, so an 'archived' point must never be allowed to overwrite a measured one and the chart must separate the two.
ideas.why: A badge's earliest weeks decide its rarity, and that is exactly the data a young database does not have.

ideas.title: Badge art alt-text generation
ideas.body: Generate a short factual description of each badge's artwork (dominant shapes, colours, any text inside the art) and store it as the alt text used by the grid tile, the detail image and the OG card, with an admin override per badge. Runs as a pass over newly added badges in the sync. Effort: M. Risk if built badly: a confident wrong description ('a red heart') is worse for screen-reader users than a neutral fallback, so anything ungenerated or low-confidence must fall back to 'badge titled X'.
ideas.why: The catalog is a wall of images with no words, and screen-reader users meet the wall first.

ideas.title: Localized badge metadata layer
ideas.body: Add a translation table keyed on badge id and on provider category terms, holding name, short description and category label per locale, with fallback to the provider's English string when a translation is missing. The badge page, catalog facets, OG card and feeds all read through it, and the admin view shows per-locale fill so an untranslated row is visibly untranslated rather than silently English. Effort: L. Risk if built badly: machine-translating badge names produces plausible nonsense that then outranks the correct English in search, so every term must carry a human or machine marker and machine output must not be indexed as canonical.
ideas.why: Eleven locales of interface chrome around English badge names is only half a localized catalog.

ideas.title: Badge head-to-head comparison
ideas.body: Pick any two badges and see them head to head: owner curves on one axis, windows drawn as bars, each rarity signal as a diverging bar, and a written diff ('opens three days earlier, four times fewer owners, one tier higher'), shareable by URL with both ids. Uses the catalog, badge_stats and window history. Effort: M. Risk if built badly: overlaying two curves with different observation spans makes the younger badge look flat, so each side must state its measured coverage and estimated spans must be drawn distinctly.
ideas.why: Collectors argue about which badge is harder or better and there is nowhere to settle it with data.

ideas.title: Versioned rarity methodology page
ideas.body: Publish the TBRI formula exactly as implemented, with one real badge's numbers worked through it step by step, the formula version, and the change history of that version so a score from six months ago can still be explained. The numbers are computed live from a stable badge through the same module the syncs use, never hard-coded into the page. Effort: S. Risk if built badly: a worked example with hard-coded values breaks silently as the catalog changes, so it must be generated live and covered by a test that fails when the page and the formula disagree.
ideas.why: Rarity is the site's central claim and a versioned public formula is the difference between a metric and a mystery.

ideas.title: Badge art pack export
ideas.body: From a category, a set page or your own inventory, generate a downloadable pack: one sprite sheet of the selected art at 1x, 2x and 4x plus a JSON manifest mapping each tile to its badge id, title and source URL. Built for streamers, emote tools and Discord bots that otherwise re-download badge art file by file. Effort: M. Risk if built badly: redistributing Twitch art without attribution is a terms problem, so the manifest must carry the source URL and a usage note on every pack.
ideas.why: Everyone building a Twitch tool needs badge art in bulk and the catalog only offers single images.

ideas.title: Live claimability probe
ideas.body: A cron walks every badge currently marked claimable, opens the provider page and, where available, the Twitch claim path, and records whether it still presents as claimable, stamping 'verified live at HH:MM' on the card and badge page. A badge the feed calls open but the probe cannot confirm drops to a 'not verified' state instead of showing a confident countdown. Effort: M. Risk if built badly: probing looks like scraping and will be rate-limited or blocked, so it must reuse the polite fetch wrapper, honour Retry-After and back off rather than hammering a provider.
ideas.why: A countdown that leads to a dead claim page is the fastest way to lose a visitor's trust.

ideas.title: Community tags on badges
ideas.body: Any logged-in member can add short free-form tags to a badge ('nostalgia', 'ugly', 'subscribe-and-forget') from a suggestion list, and each tag gets a page listing every badge carrying it, ordered by rarity, plus a tag cloud on the catalog. Moderation reuses the existing admin content tools; no other list on the site is a shared vocabulary over the catalog. Effort: M. Risk if built badly: an unshaped folksonomy fills up with synonyms and insults, so tags need normalization, a report control and a merge tool for duplicates.
ideas.why: Collectors describe badges in their own words and the catalog only offers Twitch's provider categories.

ideas.title: Pixel-art crisp rendering policy
ideas.body: Detect badges whose art is upscaled pixel art (blocky edges, small palette, nearest-neighbour scaling artefacts) and apply a per-badge rendering policy so those tiles and detail images scale with nearest-neighbour rather than smoothing, storing the flag alongside the badge. A catalog-wide 'crisp render' pass fixes blurry pixel badges at every size already displayed, with no new asset needed. Effort: S. Risk if built badly: a wrong flag makes a smooth badge look jagged, so the detector needs a manual override and should only switch rendering where confidence is high.
ideas.why: Most Twitch badge art is pixel art and the site currently blurs all of it at the sizes people actually see.

ideas.title: Category contradiction flagger
ideas.body: Derive a probable category from each badge's set_id and name patterns, then flag rows whose provider category contradicts the pattern ('set_id says Subscriber, provider says Prime Gaming') in an admin queue with a one-click accept and a rule-version history. Recurring contradictions become rules rather than one-off fixes. Effort: M. Risk if built badly: rules overfit one provider's naming and mislabel genuine variants, so every suggestion must be reviewed and the rule set versioned with an undo.
ideas.why: Category is the catalog's main browse axis and it is provider-supplied and demonstrably inconsistent.

ideas.title: Set completion board
ideas.body: For every set_id, compute what share of tracked members hold every version, show the set's completion share on its page and on each badge page, and publish an exhibit of sets nobody has completed with the single version that blocks them most often. Uses synced inventories against the set's version list. Effort: M. Risk if built badly: with a small member base most sets read as 0 percent, so the share must always show its denominator and the exhibit must require a minimum member count before naming a set.
ideas.why: Sets are the natural unit of badge collecting and the catalog has no notion of how close anyone is to one.

ideas.title: Hash-chained first-sighting registry
ideas.body: Append every badge's first observation as an entry that hashes the previous entry, and expose a public page plus a JSON endpoint that verifies a badge's entry against the chain, so anyone can prove when this site first saw a badge and that the record was not rewritten afterwards. Effort: L. Risk if built badly: a chain over a dataset that still legitimately gets corrected (merged rows, renamed badges) must support explicit, chained amendments instead of pretending history never changed.
ideas.why: Leak claims and rarity history are only worth citing if the observation log cannot be edited later.

ideas.title: Badge search alias table
ideas.body: A curated alias table maps colloquial names to badges and categories ('prime', 'turbo', 'twitchcon 2019', 'sub badge'), so search resolves them instead of returning nothing; the admin adds aliases, sees which are actually used, and each badge page shows 'also known as'. Feeds the existing search and the catalog facets. Effort: S. Risk if built badly: an alias pointing at the wrong set produces confident wrong answers, so the result page must state which alias matched and let the user correct it.
ideas.why: Nobody searches with Twitch's internal set names, they search with what the badge is called in chat.

ideas.title: Badge art asset audit
ideas.body: A pass records which resolutions exist for each badge (1x, 2x, 4x), the byte size, and whether the canonical URL still returns an image, then publishes a 'blurry' and a 'broken art' filter with an admin list of badges whose art is missing or dead. Dead URLs get a single re-resolve attempt against the catalog before they are recorded as broken, and missing higher resolutions get a distinct placeholder treatment instead of an upscaled blur. Effort: S. Risk if built badly: a transient CDN failure marks hundreds of badges broken, so failures need a retry and a cool-down before they are stored.
ideas.why: A catalog judged on its artwork should know which of its images are missing, dead or low-resolution.

ideas.title: Ghost median-curve overlay
ideas.body: Draw a badge's owner curve against a ghost line: the median curve of comparable badges in the same category at a similar release age, built by aligning every series at age zero and taking the median per age bucket. The chart then reads ahead of the typical TwitchCon badge instead of a bare number, and the gap at 30 and 90 days becomes a comparable score. Effort: M. Risk if built badly: the baseline mixes badges with different window lengths and provider coverage, so a minimum cohort size must be enforced and shown or the ghost line misleads.
ideas.why: An owner count means nothing without a comparison, and the catalog already holds thousands of comparable curves.

ideas.title: Cross-script search matching
ideas.body: Index a transliterated form of every catalog name so a query typed in Japanese, Arabic or Cyrillic script, or in Latin transliteration of a non-Latin name, still finds the badge, and show in the result which form matched. Built as an additional index beside the existing search, never replacing it. Effort: M. Risk if built badly: aggressive transliteration creates false matches on short names, so results must display the matched form so a wrong hit is obvious immediately.
ideas.why: Gateway and ゲートウェイ are the same badge and the catalog currently answers only one of them.

ideas.title: Verified claim attestation
ideas.body: For badges the automated ownership sync cannot see (regional, in-game, event-only), a member submits an attestation with a screenshot and a note; an admin or a quorum of high-trust members verifies it, and it then counts in that member's inventory under a distinct 'attested' mark that is shown separately from sync-verified ownership wherever counts are used. Effort: L. Risk if built badly: a gameable verification path inflates rarity statistics, so attested ownership must never silently mix into the verified counts that drive TBRI.
ideas.why: There is no official per-user badge API, so a real slice of ownership is invisible to every sync.

ideas.title: Badge rename tracker
ideas.body: Detect when a provider renames a badge or set across syncs, keep the old name, and show a 'formerly known as' line on the detail page with the rename date while the retired name stays in the search index so old links and old habits still resolve. Writes a changelog row per rename. Effort: S. Risk if built badly: matching names across syncs by list position rather than by id invents a rename every time a provider reorders its output, so matching must be id-first.
ideas.why: Names change, bookmarks and memory do not, and nothing in the catalog records the change.

ideas.title: Paid-badge cost archive
ideas.body: A curated table records what the badges that required real money cost at release (charity badges, Turbo, paid campaigns) with their currency and region variants, and shows a cost line on the badge page beside its free or paid status, plus a catalog filter and a total for a category. Prices come from the admin table and provider notes, never invented. Effort: M. Risk if built badly: mixing currencies and regions into one number produces a confident wrong figure, so each price must carry its currency, region and source date, or it must not be shown.
ideas.why: A meaningful slice of the catalog cost real money and the catalog records only the word paid.

ideas.title: Catalog diff since last visit
ideas.body: Store a last-visit timestamp per member and add a 'changed since you last looked' filter to the catalog showing badges added, windows opened or closed, tier crossings and art revisions since that moment, with a count chip on the grid and a plain summary in the empty state. Falls back to seven days on a first visit. Uses badge_events, window history and the tier series. Effort: M. Risk if built badly: a rare visitor gets an overwhelming diff, so it needs a cap, a summary header and grouping by change type rather than a raw list.
ideas.why: The catalog changes every day and a returning collector has no way to see what moved while they were away.

ideas.title: Claim plan for open windows
ideas.body: A member gets a persistent claim plan: the open windows they care about, ordered by a server-computed combination of deadline and rarity, each with a state of want, claimed or skipped that survives across visits and devices, plus a progress ring and an exportable checklist. It is stateful per member, unlike the stateless claimable filter, and it is silent, unlike wishlist alerts. Uses open windows, member wishlist data and synced ownership to auto-tick claims that landed. Effort: M. Risk if built badly: if a claimed tick depends on the next inventory sync rather than the member, the plan shows false progress, so the manual state and the synced state must be stored and displayed separately.
ideas.why: Collectors juggling several live windows need a plan they can trust across days, not a fresh filter every visit.

ideas.title: Zero-result search gap report
ideas.body: Log anonymous search queries that return no results (query text, locale, timestamp, no identifier) and roll them into a 'missing from the catalog' report ranked by frequency, where each row is triaged as a real badge the catalog lacks, a missing alias, or a typo, with the fix action attached. Feeds the alias table and the admin badge queue. Effort: M. Risk if built badly: query text is personal data, so the log needs a documented short retention window and must store no identifier at all.
ideas.why: Every failed search is a visitor who wanted a badge the catalog could not name.

ideas.title: Rare badge combination detector
ideas.body: Mine synced inventories for pairs and triples of badges that almost never co-occur because their windows were years apart or their audiences differ, and publish the hardest combinations with the few members who hold them (opt-in only). It is the inverse of recommendations: not what to chase next, but which combinations are nearly impossible. Effort: L. Risk if built badly: with few synced memberships, absent co-occurrence is just missing data, so a combination needs a minimum observation base before it can be called impossible.
ideas.why: The rare badge is common knowledge, the rare combination is the actual flex.

ideas.title: Provisional rarity labelling
ideas.body: Badges younger than a configurable observation window, or backed by fewer than N owner samples, show their TBRI as 'provisional' with a distinct chip, are excluded from tier-crossing alerts and tier-based leaderboards until they mature, and the detail page states when the estimate should settle. Uses the age of the badge's badge_stats series. Effort: M. Risk if built badly: hiding provisional badges instead of labelling them removes new drops from the catalog at exactly the moment people are searching for them.
ideas.why: Rarity computed from three days of data is a guess, and presenting it as a tier misleads everyone who reads it.

ideas.title: Co-release bundle detection
ideas.body: Detect badges whose claim windows open within the same short interval and publish them as a bundle: a page per cluster with its badges, the shared window and combined owner base, plus a 'drops together' chip on each member badge. Uses window history only, and gives collectors one object to track instead of five separate countdowns. Effort: M. Risk if built badly: a generous interval collapses the whole catalog into one bundle, so the threshold needs tuning and each bundle must show why its members were grouped.
ideas.why: Twitch releases badges in batches and the catalog forces collectors to track them one by one.

ideas.title: Status contradiction watch
ideas.body: A nightly check flags badges whose stored status contradicts the evidence: marked active but unlisted by every provider for N days, or window open but zero new owners across M consecutive syncs, or end date long past with status still active. Each flag shows a small 'status uncertain' mark on the badge with the evidence sentence attached and lands in an admin queue. Effort: M. Risk if built badly: a genuinely quiet badge in a quiet week is not broken, so the check must require both provider silence and owner stalling before it raises a flag.
ideas.why: A wrong status is worse than an unknown one, because a countdown reads as a promise.

ideas.title: Timezone fairness index per window
ideas.body: Score every claim window by how much of the world was awake at its open and close: weight the window's hours against a population-by-timezone curve and produce an index plus a plain label such as closes at 03:00 for Europe. Window pages and the drop list can sort by it, and the catalog can call out windows that only ever opened during one hemisphere's daytime. Effort: S. Risk if built badly: the population curve is an approximation and the score can read as a fairness verdict on Twitch, so present it as a planning aid and always show the underlying hour table so anyone can check it.
ideas.why: A large part of the audience loses drops to the clock and a window-level score is the only way to see that pattern in the data.

ideas.title: Community ownership share
ideas.body: For every badge, compute the share of this site's synced members who own it, show it on the detail page beside the global owner count, and use it as a catalog sort. It is a second, independent rarity signal that still works where potat returns nothing, and it can be labelled honestly as a lower bound ('at least N of our members hold this'). Effort: M. Risk if built badly: the member base is small and self-selected, so the share must be presented as site-relative with its denominator visible and never as a claim about global ownership.
ideas.why: A second ownership signal is what makes the site's rarity numbers defensible when one provider goes quiet.

ideas.title: Rarity tier cutoff calibration audit
ideas.body: Recompute the live distribution of TBRI values and check that the tier cutoffs still produce the pyramid the tiers claim: how many Legendaries actually exist, whether a band is empty or overflowing, and what share of the catalog sits in each tier. Publishes the cutoff table, the current shares and a proposed recut when the distribution has drifted, stored per run so the drift is visible over time. Effort: S. Risk if built badly: automatic recuts would invalidate every screenshot and ranking overnight, so the audit may only propose; cutoffs change deliberately and are versioned.
ideas.why: Rarity tiers are the catalog's shared vocabulary and nothing currently checks that the labels still match the thresholds defining them.

ideas.title: set_id reverse lookup
ideas.body: A small page plus a JSON endpoint where anyone pastes a Twitch set_id, a full badge UUID or an image URL and gets the catalog entry with its set page, current status and owner count, with redirects so a raw id URL behaves like a badge page. Built for Discord bot authors, wiki editors and moderators who hold an id and nothing else. Effort: S. Risk if built badly: an id resolver that falls back to the nearest match returns the wrong badge with confidence, so unknown ids must return a clean not-found rather than a guess.
ideas.why: Developers and moderators work in set_ids while the catalog only speaks badge names.

ideas.title: Text-in-art OCR search
ideas.body: Extract the text drawn inside badge artwork (years, campaign names, letters) into an indexed field at sync time, let catalog search match it so a query for 2019 or hype finds badges whose art literally carries those words, and show the extracted words on the detail page as 'text in art' with an admin correction. Effort: M. Risk if built badly: OCR on 24 px art is unreliable, so low-confidence extractions must not be indexed and any wrong text must be correctable without touching the image.
ideas.why: Badge art is full of legible text that the catalog currently ignores entirely.

ideas.title: Structured catalog query language
ideas.body: A documented predicate grammar over the catalog: cat:twitchcon year:2024 owners:<500 window:open -owned tier:legendary, parsed server-side into parameterized PostgREST filters, with every filter state exposing a copy-as-query button and a shareable URL, and named queries a member can save and reopen. A short syntax reference sits under the search box. It filters the catalog and is deliberately separate from the matching-based search (alias, cross-script, text-in-art), which answers a different question. Effort: M. Risk if built badly: a hand-rolled parser over user input is an injection and denial-of-service surface if it reaches SQL unchecked, so fields and operators must be allow-listed and only parameterized filters emitted.
ideas.why: The catalog holds the answer to thousands of precise questions and a predicate language is the only interface that can ask them.

ideas.title: Measured vs estimated owner series
ideas.body: Mark every point in a badge's owner curve as measured or estimated: gaps between observations render as dashed interpolated spans showing the gap length, and any badge with more estimated than measured span carries a 'sparse history' note on the chart and its rarity chip. Uses the sync timestamp recorded on each badge_stats row. Effort: S. Risk if built badly: interpolation that looks like data is how a chart lies, so estimated spans must be visually distinct and excluded from any slope-based statistic.
ideas.why: Half of a young owner curve is interpolation and nothing in the interface currently says so.

ideas.title: Catalog scope and exclusions page
ideas.body: A public page documenting what this database deliberately leaves out: the status and role badge classes (moderator, VIP, partner, prime, turbo, staff and their siblings) with live counts pulled from Helix, the reason each is not a collectible catalog entry, and a read-only reference gallery of their current art so the many visitors who come looking for mod or VIP badge art find it and understand the boundary. The exclusion rule is derived from the same check the sync uses, so the page can never disagree with what is stored. Effort: S. Risk if built badly: mixing the reference gallery into normal catalog surfaces, search or the grid re-admits exactly the rows the catalog is built to exclude, so the page must be isolated from every catalog query and clearly labelled as reference.
ideas.why: Status badges are the single most searched class this catalog refuses to hold and the refusal is currently invisible.

ideas.title: Evergreen vs limited lifecycle
ideas.body: Derive a lifecycle state per badge, never yet closed (evergreen, like subscriber badges), closed at least once (limited), or returned (reissued), show it as a chip on the tile and detail page, and add it to the catalog facets so permanent and limited are browsable classes. Distinct from the claimable-now filter, which only sees today's state. Effort: M. Risk if built badly: a limited badge that simply has not closed yet is mislabelled evergreen, so the chip must say 'no recorded end' whenever that is all the data supports.
ideas.why: Whether a badge is permanent or a one-time drop is the first question a collector asks about it.

ideas.title: Catalog records board
ideas.body: A records page computed over the whole catalog: fastest to 100k owners, longest continuously open window, largest set by version count, rarest badge still claimable, oldest badge still obtainable, biggest single-sync owner jump, most owners lost to a provider revision. Each record links to the badge and states the observation window it was computed over, with the date it was set. Effort: M. Risk if built badly: records over a short history are artefacts of when this site started syncing, so every record must disclose its window or it will silently mean 'since we launched'.
ideas.why: The catalog contains superlatives nobody has ever computed and records are readable at a glance.

ideas.title: Unknown-deadline honesty state
ideas.body: Badges with no listed end date get an explicit 'no known deadline' state instead of an implied permanent one: no countdown, no urgency styling, a note that the deadline is unknown with the date we last looked, and a slot in an admin research queue of badges whose deadline is missing. Each badge records whether its deadline is listed, inferred from past windows, or unknown. Effort: S. Risk if built badly: silently treating unknown as permanent gives false safety on a badge that may close tomorrow, so the state must be visibly different from an evergreen badge.
ideas.why: An unknown deadline rendered as no deadline is the catalog's most expensive small lie.

ideas.title: Claim funnel per badge
ideas.body: Instrument the badge page as a small funnel: page views, expand of the claim instructions, clicks on the claim link, and confirmed owned-afterwards from the next inventory sync, all from anonymous analytics plus link-click logging, with an admin view of the badges with the most interest and the fewest conversions. It answers which badges people want and cannot get. Effort: M. Risk if built badly: tiny per-badge samples read as trends, so the funnel must show counts, suppress below a threshold and aggregate over weeks rather than days.
ideas.why: Whether a badge page turns interest into a claimed badge is the catalog's own conversion question.
